title: Futur simple
description: Say what will happen with one-word future forms.
rule: Form the futur simple from the infinitive plus the endings -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont: je parlerai, nous finirons. Verbs ending in -re drop the final e first: prendre → je prendrai. Some common verbs have an irregular stem with the same endings: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-, venir → viendr-, pouvoir → pourr-, vouloir → voudr-, devoir → devr-, savoir → saur-, voir → verr-, envoyer → enverr-, and il faut → il faudra, il pleut → il pleuvra. Some -er verbs change spelling in the stem: acheter → j’achèterai, appeler → j’appellerai, payer → je paierai or je payerai. After quand, a future event takes the futur simple, where English uses the present: quand j’arriverai, je t’appellerai. Time markers such as demain, l’année prochaine and dans dix ans point to the future.
example: Demain, je finirai ce livre. · Quand tu viendras, nous irons au cinéma. · Il pleuvra ce week-end.
aside: For near plans, speakers often use the futur proche (je vais partir); the futur simple is common for more distant or more formal plans, and after quand for a future event.

exercises.hint: Keep the whole infinitive and add the nous ending.
exercises.feedback: The futur simple starts from the full infinitive, then adds the ending for the person.
exercises.explanation: Parler + -ons gives nous parlerons.

exercises.hint: Start from finir and add the ils ending.
exercises.feedback: Check the ending: the ils form of the future ends in -ont.
exercises.explanation: Finir + -ont gives ils finiront.

exercises.instruction: Write choisir in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: Keep the full infinitive and add the tu ending.
exercises.feedback: The tu ending of the future is -as, added to the whole infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Choisir + -as gives tu choisiras.

exercises.hint: All four are future forms. Which ending goes with vous?
exercises.feedback: Match the ending to the subject vous.
exercises.explanation: Vous takes the ending -ez: vous inviterez.

exercises.source: Nous mangerez à la maison demain.
answers: Nous mangerons à la maison demain.
exercises.hint: Look at the ending of the verb and at the subject.
exercises.feedback: The verb ending does not match nous.
exercises.explanation: With nous, the future ending is -ons: nous mangerons.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence in the futur simple.
exercises.source: I will talk to my sister tonight.
answers: Je parlerai à ma sœur ce soir.
exercises.hint: Two tiles are future forms of parler. Only one matches je.
exercises.feedback: Check which future ending belongs with je.
exercises.explanation: Je takes the ending -ai: je parlerai. Parleras is the tu form.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: Start from the infinitive of the verb and add the il ending.
exercises.feedback: The future is built on the full infinitive travailler.
exercises.explanation: Travailler + -a gives il travaillera.

exercises.hint: Verbs ending in -re lose one letter before the ending.
exercises.feedback: Remove the final e of prendre before adding the ending.
exercises.explanation: Prendre loses its e: prendr- + -ai gives je prendrai.

exercises.instruction: Write attendre in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: Drop the final e of the infinitive, then add the nous ending.
exercises.feedback: An -re verb keeps its r but not its final e in the future.
exercises.explanation: Attendre becomes attendr-, and nous adds -ons: nous attendrons.

exercises.source: Elle ____ un livre dans le train.
exercises.hint: The verb is lire. What happens to its final e?
exercises.feedback: The future of an -re verb starts from the infinitive without its e.
exercises.explanation: Lire becomes lir-, and elle adds -a: elle lira.

exercises.hint: Look at the stem of the verb: one letter is too many.
exercises.feedback: An -re verb drops its final e before the future ending.
exercises.explanation: Prendre becomes prendr-, so the ils form is ils prendront.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: The infinitive is vendre. Remove its last letter, then add the tu ending.
exercises.feedback: Build the future on vendr-, not on the present form.
exercises.explanation: Vendre becomes vendr-, and tu adds -as: tu vendras.

alternatives.message: This topic practises the futur simple. Your answer uses the futur proche (aller + infinitive), which is also correct French, but write the one-word future form here.

exercises.hint: Prendre is an -re verb, so its future stem loses the e.
exercises.feedback: Use the one-word future of prendre with nous.
exercises.explanation: Prendre becomes prendr-, and nous adds -ons: nous prendrons. On prendra is also correct.

exercises.hint: Être has its own future stem, which does not look like the infinitive.
exercises.feedback: Être uses the stem ser- in the future.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of être is ser-, so tu seras.

exercises.hint: Aller has a very short, irregular future stem.
exercises.feedback: The future of aller is not built on aller-.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of aller is ir-, so nous irons.

exercises.instruction: Write avoir in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: Avoir has an irregular future stem. The je ending is -ai.
exercises.feedback: The future stem of avoir is not av-.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of avoir is aur-, so j’aurai.

exercises.hint: Faire has an irregular future stem. Also check the ending for ils.
exercises.feedback: Look for the irregular stem of faire together with the ils ending.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of faire is fer-, and ils adds -ont: ils feront.

exercises.hint: Avoir does not build its future on av-.
exercises.feedback: The stem of the verb is wrong: avoir is irregular in the future.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of avoir is aur-, so tu auras.

exercises.source: They (masculine) will have a big house.

alternatives.answer: Ils vont avoir une grande maison.
alternatives.message: This topic practises the futur simple. Your answer uses the futur proche (aller + infinitive), which is also correct French, but write the one-word future form here.

alternatives.answer: Ils vont avoir une grosse maison.

exercises.hint: Use the irregular future stem of avoir with the ils ending.
exercises.feedback: Avoir has an irregular future stem.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of avoir is aur-, and ils adds -ont: ils auront.

exercises.hint: Venir has an irregular future stem with a d in it.
exercises.feedback: The future of venir is not built on venir-.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of venir is viendr-, so elle viendra.

exercises.hint: Vouloir has an irregular future stem with a d in it.
exercises.feedback: The future of vouloir is not built on vouloir-.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of vouloir is voudr-, so vous voudrez.

exercises.instruction: Write falloir in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: Falloir only exists with il. Its future stem is irregular.
exercises.feedback: Il faut becomes something quite different in the future.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of falloir is faudr-, so il faudra.

exercises.hint: The verb is pleuvoir. Its future stem is short and irregular.
exercises.feedback: Pleuvoir loses the oi of its infinitive in the future: pleuv- + r.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of pleuvoir is pleuvr-, so il pleuvra. Pleura is a form of pleurer, to cry.

exercises.source: Je t’____ une photo ce soir.
exercises.hint: Envoyer has an irregular future stem with a double r.
exercises.feedback: The future of envoyer is not built on the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of envoyer is enverr-, so j’enverrai.

exercises.hint: Pouvoir has an irregular future stem with a double r.
exercises.feedback: The stem of pouvoir is wrong.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of pouvoir is pourr-, so vous pourrez.

exercises.hint: Voir has an irregular future stem with a double r.
exercises.feedback: The future of voir is not built on voir-.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of voir is verr-, so nous verrons. On verra is also correct.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence in the futur simple.
exercises.source: You will know the truth tomorrow.
exercises.hint: Savoir has an irregular future stem. One tile is a wrong form.
exercises.feedback: Only one of the two verb tiles is a real future form of savoir.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of savoir is saur-, so vous saurez.

exercises.instruction: Write the verb form. Watch the accent.
exercises.hint: Acheter changes its first e in the future, as in j’achète.
exercises.feedback: The stem of acheter needs a grave accent in the future.
exercises.explanation: Acheter takes a grave accent: j’achèterai.

exercises.hint: Appeler changes its stem in every future form, as in j’appelle.
exercises.feedback: Appeler doubles a letter in the future stem.
exercises.explanation: Appeler doubles its l in the future: nous appellerons.

exercises.instruction: Write payer in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: Payer may change its y in the future. Add the vous ending.
exercises.feedback: Use the future stem of payer with the vous ending -ez.
exercises.explanation: Payer has two accepted future stems: vous paierez or vous payerez.

exercises.hint: Appeler keeps its double p and changes the letter after the e.
exercises.feedback: Look at the l: appeler changes it in the future.
exercises.explanation: Appeler doubles its l in the future: je t’appellerai.

exercises.instruction: Fix the spelling of the verb.
exercises.source: Nous acheterons des fruits au marché.
answers: Nous achèterons des fruits au marché.
exercises.hint: Acheter changes its stem in the future, as in j’achète.
exercises.feedback: One accent is missing in the verb.
exercises.explanation: The future stem of acheter is achèter-, with a grave accent: nous achèterons.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: Payer keeps its full stem before the future ending.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile has lost part of the stem.
exercises.explanation: Payer becomes paier- (or payer-) in the future, so ils paieront.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French. Watch the accent.
exercises.source: I will buy (acheter) a new bag.

alternatives.answer: Je vais acheter un nouveau sac.

alternatives.answer: Je vais acheter un sac neuf.

exercises.feedback: Check the accent in the stem of acheter.
exercises.explanation: Acheter takes a grave accent in the future: j’achèterai.

exercises.hint: The arrival is in the future, and the subject is tu.
exercises.feedback: After quand for a future event, French uses the futur simple.
exercises.explanation: The arrival is still to come, so quand takes the future: quand tu arriveras.

exercises.instruction: Write avoir in the futur simple.
exercises.source: Quand nous ____ (avoir) de l’argent, nous achèterons une voiture.
exercises.hint: The event after quand is in the future, so both verbs are in the future.
exercises.feedback: Use the future after quand, with the irregular stem of avoir.
exercises.explanation: After quand for a future event, use the future: quand nous aurons.

exercises.instruction: Put both verbs in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: Change the verb after quand too, not only the main verb.
exercises.feedback: Both verbs must move to the future, including the one after quand.
exercises.explanation: For a future event, French puts the verb after quand in the future as well: quand elle rentrera.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French. Start with Quand.
exercises.source: When I arrive, I will call you (to a friend).

alternatives.message: English uses the present after when, but French puts a future event after quand in the futur simple: quand j’arriverai.

exercises.hint: English says “when I arrive”, but French is more logical about the time.
exercises.feedback: The arrival is in the future, so the verb after quand is in the future too.
exercises.explanation: After quand for a future event, French uses the future: quand j’arriverai, je t’appellerai.

exercises.source: When he comes, we will eat together.
answers: Quand il viendra, nous mangerons ensemble.
exercises.hint: Two tiles are forms of venir. The coming is still in the future.
exercises.feedback: After quand for a future event, choose the future form.
exercises.explanation: The visit is in the future, so quand takes the future: quand il viendra.

exercises.instruction: Fix the verb after quand: the event is in the future.
exercises.source: Quand je finis mes études, je voyagerai en Asie.
answers: Quand je finirai mes études, je voyagerai en Asie.
exercises.hint: The main verb is already in the future. Look at the other one.
exercises.feedback: The end of the studies is in the future, like the journey.
exercises.explanation: After quand for a future event, use the future: quand je finirai mes études.

exercises.source: Dans dix ans, nous ____ une grande maison.
exercises.hint: Dans dix ans points to the future. Check the subject too.
exercises.feedback: The time marker dans dix ans needs a future verb.
exercises.explanation: Dans dix ans means in ten years’ time, so the verb is in the future: nous aurons.

exercises.instruction: Choose the time marker that fits the verb.
exercises.hint: Partirai is a future form. Which marker points forward in time?
exercises.feedback: The verb is in the future, so the time marker must be too.
exercises.explanation: Je partirai is the future, and only demain points to the future.

exercises.instruction: Write parler in the futur simple.
exercises.source: Dans dix ans, tu ____ (parler) très bien français.
exercises.hint: The time marker points forward. Add the tu ending to the full infinitive.
exercises.feedback: Dans dix ans needs the future tense.
exercises.explanation: Dans dix ans calls for the future: tu parleras.

alternatives.answer: Elles vont partir la semaine prochaine.
alternatives.message: This topic practises the futur simple. Your answer uses the futur proche (aller + infinitive), which is also correct French, but write the one-word future form here.

exercises.hint: Next week is la semaine prochaine. Partir builds its future on the infinitive.
exercises.feedback: Use the one-word future of partir with elles.
exercises.explanation: Partir + -ont gives elles partiront; la semaine prochaine can go at the start or the end.

exercises.instruction: Replace Hier with Demain and put the verb in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: The passé composé j’ai fini becomes a one-word future.
exercises.feedback: Demain needs the future, not the passé composé.
exercises.explanation: With demain, the verb moves to the future: je finirai.

exercises.instruction: Fix the verb so it matches the time marker.
exercises.source: L’année prochaine, nous visitions le Canada.
answers: L’année prochaine, nous visiterons le Canada.
exercises.hint: L’année prochaine points forward, but the verb points back.
exercises.feedback: The verb is in the imparfait, but the time marker is in the future.
exercises.explanation: L’année prochaine calls for the future: nous visiterons.
